title: Minding the spaces
idea: + joins with no gap. To get a space, you must add it yourself as part of a string.

exercises.explanation: + adds no space. The words crash together: HarryLee. We have to add a space on purpose.

exercises.prompt:
How do we get a space between the words?

print("Harry" + ____ + "Lee")
exercises.explanation: A space is just text! " " is a string with one space inside. Join it in the middle.
The " " in the middle is a one-space string. Now you get: Harry Lee.

exercises.prompt: A space " " counts as text (a string), so you can join it with +.
exercises.explanation: A space is a character, so " " is a real string. You can join it just like any word.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

first = "Good"
second = "day"
print(first + " " + second)
exercises.explanation: The values are "Good" and "day", with a space string between: Good day.

exercises.prompt:
Another way to add the space: put it inside a word. What will this show?

print("Hello " + "Sam")
exercises.explanation: The space is tucked inside "Hello " (after the o). So joining gives: Hello Sam.

exercises.prompt:
Fill the blank so this shows: tea time

print("tea" + ____ + "time")
exercises.explanation: A one-space string " " sits between the two words to make: tea time.

exercises.prompt: Build a line that prints: red car (join red, a space, and car).
exercises.explanation: "red" + " " + "car" gives red car. The middle piece is the space.

options: There's no space, so it shows Thankyou
exercises.explanation: The words run together: Thankyou. The fix is to add a space string between them.

exercises.prompt: Why does joining strings so often forget spaces?
options: Because + joins exactly, and a space is just more text you must include
exercises.explanation: The computer only joins what you give it. If you want a space, you must put it in. Exact, as always.
